San Francisco Planning, Article 10 landmark designation: Landmark No. 175, McLaren Lodge (ordinance, Planning Commission resolution and case report)
sources.label: SF Planning, landmark designation

historical_record.description: Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 175, McLaren Lodge.

Built of sandstone to designs by Edward R. Swain, Richardsonian Romanesque with a Mission Revival touch, as the park superintendent's residence and offices — the home of John McLaren, superintendent of Golden Gate Park for 53 years, a Scottish-born gardener trained on estates and at the Royal Botanic Garden in Edinburgh who came to California in 1872.

McLaren's report to the Park Commission on the earthquake's damage recorded that the lodge "had its chimneys thrown down and some minor cracks in the walls and some plaster is broke in the upper rooms."
